correctness.rationale: A nonempty induced vertex set is connected iff it is a singleton or hits multiple parts. Subtract the empty set and, disjointly, nonsingleton subsets of each part from the full Boolean cube. For a frequency S the sum over the subsets of part i factors as a product of 1+(-1)^{1_{v in S}}, so it is 2^{n_i} for a missed part and zero otherwise. Subtracting the singleton and empty contributions gives the claimed multiplier, with the full cube term 2^N only at S=0. Orthonormal Walsh characters diagonalize the operator after unit normalization; eigenvalue magnitudes are singular values. Their common parity is N+r-1 mod 2. If N+r is odd, an all-parts-hit frequency of weight (N+r-1)/2 is feasible in [r,N] and has multiplier zero. If N+r is even, an all-parts-hit frequency of weight (N+r)/2 in [r,N] has multiplier -1, also in the complete graph edge case N=r. The zero-frequency cardinality is maximal by the triangle inequality. Each proper missed-part set defines a disjoint class, counted by the stated coefficient, and the empty character has positive multiplier. Comparing nullity with the relevant binomial layer costs at most twice the union bound sum_i 2^{N-n_i}; Stirling at a bounded offset from N/2 gives the stated relative O_r(1/N) error. Finite independent replay used graph search on each induced subset then direct integer character sums; 479 assertions for 136 nondecreasing shapes (2<=r<=6, each size <=6, N<=11) corroborated parity and the minimum invertible singular value. For (2,2), (2,3), (3,4), respectively, (nullity, maximum absolute eigenvalue) equals (0,13), (12,26), (34,112). Replay details: /workspace/reviews/evidence/5-walsh-replay.md. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed.
